subject: The Papyrus · A country on a ribbon of green
html:
Welcome to The Papyrus

One letter a month, always a number you did not know — Egypt, told through its real, cited data.

To start: about 116 million people live in Egypt, but almost all of them are crowded onto the roughly 4% of the country that the Nile and its delta keep green. The other 96% is desert. That single fact shapes nearly everything else — where the cities are, why the new capital is being built east of Cairo, and why the Nile's water is treated as a matter of national survival. (Sources: CAPMAS; World Bank.)

Another: the Suez Canal normally carries a slice of all world trade, but Red Sea shipping disruptions cut its revenue to about $3.6bn in FY2024/25, down roughly 45% year on year — a reminder that a single waterway can move a national budget. (Sources: Suez Canal Authority; Central Bank of Egypt, 2026.)

That is the whole idea of EgyBI: learn to work with data on facts that are actually true and actually interesting. If you write SQL, every one of these numbers is a challenge you can solve in your browser.

Thanks for reading — see you next month.
